transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-08
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Das (Cobalt HoS), Ethan Moore (Cobalt Platform), Rosa Hernández (Cobalt Compliance)
Shared: https://redwood.example.com/pilot/cobalt/security-deck (slide highlights)

Summary:
Quick weekly pilot checkpoint focused on security/compliance items: SSO SAML integration, audit logging format and retention, SOC2 snapshot request, KMS/encryption rotation, RBAC and admin access during pilot. Agreed on next steps for logs export, SOC2 artifacts, and scheduling SSO deep dive with Cobalt IdP team.

Topics:
- SSO / SAML handshake issues seen in test accounts
- Audit log format (timestamps, user-id, session, model id)
- Short-term retention vs long-term archival for pilot data
- SOC2 evidence packet and scope for pilot
- KMS/HSM integration and key rotation expectations

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): ok folks good afternoon, thanks for joining. we'll keep it tight 45-ish minutes on security items and a couple follow-ups, um, quick roll. maya from redwood, liam our se, and from cobalt?
[00:15] Priya Das (Cobalt): hey thanks maya, priya here. happy to go through the list. were most interested in SSO and the audit logs today.
[00:30] Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE): quick note before we dive — we pushed an audit logging patch last night that adds model_id and full request headers, though the headers occasionally truncate on long prompts, we've seen that on a couple test flows.
[00:47] Ethan Moore (Cobalt): truncation — is that by default or only if the KV cache is hit? we saw some missing session ids in the samples rosa sent, so not sure where they went.
[01:03] Maya Chen: it's not KV, it's the logging pipeline size cap — we cap log payloads to reduce noise; liam can explain the exact heuristics.
[01:12] Liam: yeah so the current pipeline compresses and then samples long payloads after 8k bytes. that was to avoid hot shards during high token flows, but we can toggle to keep full headers for pilot accounts. takes an ops flag.
[01:27] Priya: we need full headers for audits, even if large. can you produce a two-week export with everything untruncated?
[01:36] Liam: yes we can. i'll export last 14 days with raw payload blobs, timestamps in UTC, and user id mapping. expect that by friday.
[01:45] Rosa Hernández: perfect. also can we see access patterns by role? like who invoked admin endpoints vs user endpoints.
[01:53] Liam: the logs include actor.role but sometimes our classifier labels 'service' vs 'user' which mislabels automated pipeline calls — we've seen that. i'll include a note in the export about those heuristics.
[02:06] Ethan: about SSO — we attempted an IdP-initiated SAML flow with our Okta test tenant and three users failed with a redirect loop. any ideas?
[02:18] Liam: we saw similar in the staging env earlier. usually that's clock skew or assertion consumer url mismatch. did your team use the latest metadata endpoint?
[02:27] Priya: yes we used the metadata URL from the redwood console, but our IdP team rotated certs earlier this week so maybe it's that.
[02:36] Maya: ok let's do a SSO deep dive — liam to run through an assertion trace with your idp team. ideally schedule next week.
[02:44] Priya: week of 9/13 works. can liam coordinate with elias from our idp?
[02:49] Liam: sure i'll reach out.
[03:00] Rosa: a compliance question — during pilot, what data does redwood persist by default? specifically do you retain raw prompts, model outputs, and any customer tokens?
[03:12] Maya: by default we persist request/response for 30 days for troubleshooting, but you can opt into shorter retention or disable request payload persistence in pilot. outputs are stored in logs unless you set redaction rules.
[03:26] Priya: can you redact PHI-like patterns automatically or do we need to provide regex rules?
[03:33] Liam: we have a configurable redact pipeline; out of the box we redact common PII patterns (SSNs, credit cards) but PHI is trickier — we recommend customer-provided patterns for edge cases. we can also run a lightweight ML detector to flag likely PHI if you want.
[03:48] Ethan: that ML detector — is it run in-cluster or in your control plane? we need it to run inside our VPC for pilot.
[03:56] Liam: good Q — currently the detector is an optional module that can run on private deployments and on dedicated pools inside the customer's VPC. hosted default runs in redwood's control plane. for your pilot we can enable the VPC option since you're on a dedicated pool.
[04:12] Priya: nice. about encryption — we use an internal KMS with periodic rotation. can redwood integrate with our KMS?
[04:20] Maya: yes, we support Bring-Your-Own-Key via KMS APIs and HSMs for private deployments. for hosted pilots we can do envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS — you'll need to provide IAM role and key arn.
[04:33] Rosa: and log encryption at rest?
[04:36] Liam: logs at rest are AES-256 by default and can be wrapped with your KMS keys. the audit export will show encryption info for each blob.
[04:46] Priya: SOC2 — can you share a snapshot or evidence for the control environment? our auditors want to see in-scope controls for logging and change management.
[04:56] Maya: yes we have a SOC2 snapshot for 2026 with in-scope controls; it's not full cert package but it includes control narratives and evidence pointers. i'll share the redacted packet by friday.
[05:07] Ethan: will that include the runbook for incident response?
[05:11] Maya: incident runbook summary yes, full ops playbook is restricted but we can provide excerpts relevant to pilot.
[05:20] Priya: retention policy — for pilot we need 7-day retention for raw prompts and 90-day for aggregated logs; can you support that config?
[05:30] Liam: yes it's configurable per-project. for raw prompts we can set 7 days and ensure longterm aggregated metrics to 90 days. we do need to confirm backups — archive copies sometimes go to cold storage, which is 365 days by default unless changed. i'll flag that.
[05:45] Rosa: ok please ensure backups respect the pilot retention — we can't have hidden archives beyond agreed retention.
[05:52] Liam: understood, we'll include that in the export metadata.
[06:00] Maya: quick note on RBAC — during the pilot we provisioned three roles: admin, engineer, viewer. Priya, who needs admin?
[06:10] Priya: only myself and ethan for now, rosa should be viewer. eventually we'll add a compliance role.
[06:19] Ethan: for audit, how are admin actions logged? is there an immutable audit trail?
[06:25] Liam: admin actions are write-once records with signer metadata; they are append-only in our audit store. for private deployments that uses customer-provided object store and we can enable object lock if your storage supports it.
[06:40] Priya: can we get a sample of the admin-action schema?
[06:44] Liam: yes i'll attach a sample JSON in the export.
[06:49] Maya: talked about model variants earlier — any concerns about fallback to cheaper quantized variants and whether that affects QA or logging?
[06:58] Rosa: we need to record which variant served each response for compliance sampling.
[07:05] Liam: the logs include model_variant field; the earlier truncation bug sometimes stripped that but fixed in patch.
[07:13] Priya: good, ensure variant is present in every response log.
[07:18] Maya: on network isolation — you previously requested private deployment options for certain data flows?
[07:26] Ethan: yeah, for production sensitive connectors we want VLAN-level isolation and no egress to public internet. for pilot we can tolerate tunneled egress but must document.
[07:36] Liam: for dedicated pilot pools we offer VPC peering and private endpoints; we can lock egress via security groups and NAT rules.
[07:45] Priya: one remaining point — legal asked about subprocessor disclosure, who else sees logs (SRE, support)?
[07:53] Maya: during pilot, SRE on-call with redwood may access logs for troubleshooting but access is logged and requires justification. we can put tighter rules in place — for example require customer approval for direct access and use redwood anonymized traces.
[08:10] Rosa: please provide that access policy text.
[08:14] Maya: will do.
[08:18] Ethan: i noticed earlier a line in the SDK docs about 'persistUserTokens' flag. is that enabled by default?
[08:26] Liam: it's false by default; we never persist auth tokens. we persist user-id mapping for analytics, but not tokens.
[08:34] Priya: can you confirm token redaction in the logs?
[08:38] Liam: yes tokens are redacted, masked at ingestion. occasionally partial tokens appear in echo if app-level logs include them, but we can filter those in the redact pipeline.
[08:50] Maya: ok let's recap actions and timing: liam exports raw logs + admin-action schema by 9/10; maya shares SOC2 snapshot + incident runbook excerpts by 9/9; priya sends encryption rotation schedule and any specific PHI sample rules by 9/13. schedule sso deep dive for week of 9/13.
[09:10] Priya: sounds good. one ask — can we have a short retention compliance checklist so our legal team can sign off quickly?
[09:18] Rosa: yes a one-pager that lists which artifacts are retained, for how long, and where they're stored.
[09:23] Maya: we have a template, i'll fill it for the pilot and send to rosa.
[09:28] Ethan: last Q — are there known PCI concerns if we route payment data through prompts?
[09:34] Liam: we strongly recommend never sending raw card data in prompts. for payments we advise tokenization on your side and reveal only non-sensitive metadata. we can add extra redaction rules for payment tokens.
[09:46] Priya: okay thanks everyone. if there are no more Qs we'll close and follow up on next steps.
[09:53] Maya: thanks all, appreciate the thoroughness. we'll update the pilot config and share artifacts.
[10:00] (meeting ends)

End of transcript.

Notes: occasional transcription glitches — names sometimes mis-tagged as 'Maya from Redwood' or generic 'Speaker 2'. Some technical terms transcribed (KV cache, HSM) accurately, others slightly off (ockta vs okta).
